objectives.label: Put the centaur markers back up
Helped the Bracken family get home
Shared supper with the cinder wolves

facet_ford.name: The Ford Stone
facet_ford.text: Wrapped in a witch's wool sock. It rings every bell charm it passes, and won't stop.

charm_ford_witch.name: Mother Thrum's Tuned Charm
charm_ford_witch.text: A bell charm tuned to the note the stones hum. Hold it near a gem and it sings.

scene_parade.narration: The shortest road north is a parade: gem wagons up to their axles in ruts, a campfire on every rise, and centaur relay-runners weaving through it all at a canter. Then the whole parade stops. Somebody up ahead is shouting "NUMBERS! GET YOUR NUMBERS!"

choices.label: Walk up to the front and see why
Read the crowd like a book
Sniff the gem wagons

scene_parade_sniff_wagons.narration: Your dragonling sniffs the nearest gem wagon and goes very still. It smells of home: warm rock, ash, the inside of a cave. And underneath that, a hum you can feel in your teeth. Every wagon in the parade smells the same, all the way to the front.

choices.label: Walk up to the front

scene_parade_read_crowd.narration: Your kitsune reads the queue the way other people read a menu. That wagon is two places ahead of where it should be. That man is selling the same pebble twice. Those three are a family and that one only says she is. By the time you reach the front, you know the whole queue's business, and the queue does not know you know.

choices.label: Walk up to the front

scene_number_pebble.narration: The road ends at the west branch of the river, and the queue to cross it is two days long. A faun provisioner named Burdock is selling numbered pebbles out of a bucket, and honeycakes at bridge-queue prices, which means three times what they are worth. Your pebble says 412. The ford is on number 9.

choices.label: Buy a very expensive honeycake
Pocket your pebble and look around

scene_number_pebble_buy_cake.narration: Burdock sells you a honeycake the size of a coin for the price of a honeycake the size of a hat. "My lucky number," he says fondly, and means your money. It is, to be fair, a very good honeycake. You make it last three bites.

choices.label: Look around the camp

scene_three_cards.narration: Behind Burdock's stall, a kitsune in a tall hat is shuffling three cards on an upturned barrel. "Find the Sun Card, win a front-of-the-queue pebble!" Nobody ever finds the Sun Card. Her tails keep twitching every time she shuffles.

choices.label: Watch her tails and catch the trick
Wink at her, one fox to another
Offer to help her draw a crowd
Keep your coins and walk on by

check_expose.prompt: Spot where the Sun Card really goes

onSuccess.narration: Every time she shuffles, the third tail flicks the Sun Card up her sleeve. You say so, loudly and politely.

onFailure.narration: You pick the middle card with total confidence. It is a picture of a very smug fox. The crowd laughs, and so, to be fair, does she.

scene_exposed.narration: The kitsune, whose name turns out to be Tamsin Three-Cards, sighs and shakes the Sun Card out of her sleeve. The whole crowd gets their pebbles back. The drovers at the front of the queue have noticed you, and drovers remember faces.

choices.label: Head for the smell of soup

scene_join_con.narration: You stand in the crowd and gasp very loudly every time somebody almost wins. Tamsin pays you with a front-of-the-queue pebble and a wink. It is shiny and it says number 1, and it is absolutely not fair.

choices.label: Head for the smell of soup

scene_soup_line.narration: At the edge of camp, people in dark robes with little crystals on strings are giving away soup to anyone whose season has gone wrong. A cheerful ladler named Wend fills your bowls without asking a single question. "Kindness first," says Wend. "Always." The crystal on Wend's string is humming, very faintly.

choices.label: Say thank you and eat up
Ask why the crystal is humming

scene_soup_line_ask_crystal.narration: Wend lifts the crystal and looks at it as if it has only just started. "It's done that since the red night," Wend says. "Whenever a gem wagon passes. We think it's trying to say something." Wend tucks it back inside the robe, where it goes on humming against Wend's heart.

choices.label: See what the queue needs

scene_soup_line_thank_wend.narration: "Thank you," you say. Wend beams and fills your bowls a second time, without asking, and remembers all your names after hearing them once. "Kindness first," says Wend again, as if it is a rule the whole world ought to have. The crystal on the string hums, very faintly, the whole time.

choices.label: See what the queue needs

choice_tolls.narration: Two days is a long time to stand in a line, and the rush is charging its own tolls. A wagon is stuck to its axles in mud. A centaur marker line has been knocked flat by queue-jumpers. And a faun family called the Brackens is sitting beside a cracked cart wheel, very quiet. Everybody vote.

choices.label: Un-mire the stuck wagon
Put the centaur markers back up
Fly the marker line and spot every post
Sit down with the Brackens

check_unmire.prompt: Heave a gem wagon out of the mud

onSuccess.narration: One, two, THREE, and the wagon comes out with a noise like a giant boot leaving a puddle. The drover gives you a brave whistle and calls you all "mudlarks", which is a compliment.

onFailure.narration: The wagon comes out in the end, but only after everyone has sat down in the mud at least once. You will be finding mud in your ears until next week.

check_markers.prompt: Put the markers back in the right order

onSuccess.narration: Post by post, you walk the line back into order, reading the worn numbers with your thumbs where the paint has gone. The last marker goes in with a thump, and the whole line points, straight and plain, at the one safe way down to the ford.

onFailure.narration: You put them all back up, beautifully, in the wrong order. A centaur runner gallops past, stops, laughs, and fixes them in about four seconds.

scene_markers_restored.narration: The marker line stands straight again, every post pointing the safe way to the ford. A centaur relay-runner slows down just long enough to say "The relay remembers," and then she is gone, already singing it to the next runner up the road.

choices.label: Back to camp before dusk

scene_family.narration: The Brackens' cart wheel is cracked, their season is over, and they need to get home before the river rises. The littlest Bracken is holding a queue pebble with a big number on it and trying very hard not to cry about it.

choices.label: Swap pebbles, so they cross before you
Share your honeycake
Lash the wheel together with rope

scene_family_fix_wheel.narration: You lash the cracked wheel together with rope, round and round, until it looks like a wheel wearing a jumper. It turns. It wobbles, but it turns. The littlest Bracken rides on top of the cart to test it and declares it the best wheel ever made, which is not true, but it will get them home.

choices.label: Back to camp before dark

scene_family_share_cake.narration: You break the honeycake into four, then five, so the littlest Bracken gets a bit from everyone. For a while nobody says anything, because honeycake. Then the mother says their season was not all bad, really, and the littlest one falls asleep against a cart wheel with crumbs on both cheeks.

choices.label: Back to camp before dark

scene_family_give_pebble.narration: You hand the littlest Bracken your pebble, and take theirs. Their number is enormous. Yours was not. The littlest Bracken looks at the small number for a long time and then stops trying not to cry and just cries, happily, all over it. The Brackens will cross at dawn, and they do not stop thanking you until dusk.

choices.label: Back to camp before dark

scene_dusk_wolves.narration: At dusk, cinder wolves come and sit just past the firelight, cold and thin, with a faint warm glow under their fur. They are not hunting. They are pointedly not sitting anywhere near the gem wagons. Every campfire in the queue is arguing about whether to feed them.

choices.label: Share your supper with them
Leave them be and keep your fire small
Shoo them away from the camp

scene_wolves_fed.narration: You put your supper down on a flat stone and step back. The wolves eat politely, and then the whole pack lies down in a heap by your fire, glowing like a pile of coals. It is the warmest night anybody in the queue has had all week. The road will remember this.

choices.label: Visit the witch's stall

encounter_wolves.narration: The wolves do not want to leave. They are cold, and your fire is right there.

onVictory.narration: The pack slinks off down the queue to the next fire, where somebody feeds them. The whole campsite hears about who shooed and who shared.

onDefeat.narration: The wolves win the argument, eat everybody's supper, and curl up on your bedrolls. You spend a long, cold night sitting up, and nobody gets much sleep.

scene_witch_stall.narration: Down the queue there is a remedy stall with a pointed hat hanging off the corner. Every time a gem wagon rolls past, all the little bell charms on the stall ring by themselves, and the witch behind the counter winces. Her name is Mother Thrum. She looks at you over her spectacles. "What do you actually want?"

choices.label: Ask her a real question: why are the charms ringing?
Ask for something for sore feet

scene_witch_stall_sore_feet.narration: Mother Thrum hands you a sunbloom draught without looking, because sore feet are the one thing everybody in a queue wants. Then she looks. "That's a want," she says. "It isn't the want." She raises one eyebrow and waits to see if you have a better question.

choices.label: Ask a better question

scene_tuned_charm.narration: "Better question than most," says Mother Thrum, and she hands you one bell charm she has tuned to the note the stones are humming. Hold it near a gem and it sings. The note is older than the road, she says, and the centaurs will tell you the road was here before everything. On her shelf, wrapped in a thick wool sock, is a stone that will not stop ringing.

choices.label: Answer her question, truly
Tell her where it fell from, and promise to take it home
Leave the stone in its sock

scene_tuned_charm_leave_it.narration: You leave the stone in its sock on her shelf. Mother Thrum nods, not surprised, and tucks the wool tighter round it. "Then it rings another night," she says. "And so do I." The charms on the stall all chime once, softly, as a wagon rolls past in the dark.

choices.label: Settle in for the night

scene_tuned_charm_take_it_home.narration: You tell her where it fell from, and that you mean to take it back. Mother Thrum unwraps the sock. The ringing stops the moment the stone touches your dragonling's hands, as if it has recognized the smell of home. "There," she says softly. "It knows." She gives you the sock as well. "Keep it warm."

choices.label: Settle in for the night

check_answer.prompt: Tell Mother Thrum what you actually want, and mean it

onSuccess.narration: Mother Thrum listens all the way to the end, then hands you the sock with the stone in it. "That's the Ford Stone. Take it somewhere it stops ringing," she says. "I'd like some sleep."

onFailure.narration: You say something about gems and glory, and Mother Thrum's charms all go quiet at once, which feels like an answer. "Not yet," she says kindly. "Ask yourself again at the mountain."

rest_witch_fire.narration: You sleep in the queue with three hundred strangers, a lot of snoring, and somebody's goat. The little tuned charm chimes softly every time a gem wagon creaks past in the dark. Queues move at night, it turns out, because drovers never sleep. In the morning, a drover is shouting numbers, and the ford is a great deal closer than it was.

choices.label: Go down to the ford

choice_ford.narration: The ford is wide and brown and fast. The drovers cross with ceremony: one wagon at a time, slow and steady, while the lead drover sings the crossing verse. Behind you, the whole queue is watching.

choices.label: Cross with the caravans, at the drovers' pace
The drovers you helped wave you in beside the lead wagon
Follow the marker line you put back up
Ride across on the Brackens' cart
Use Tamsin's front-of-the-queue pebble

check_ford.prompt: Keep your footing in the ford

onSuccess.narration: Step, wait, step. The water pushes and pulls and you do not let it. The lead drover sings the last line of the verse just as your boots hit the north bank.

onFailure.narration: Halfway across, somebody behind you shouts, and then everybody behind you shouts, and the water that was pushing at your knees is suddenly pushing at your waist.

onSuccess.narration: With friends on every side, the ford is just very wet walking. Somebody up on a wagon starts clapping as you reach the north bank.

onFailure.narration: You are nearly across, with friends on every side, when a yell goes up behind you and the whole river seems to lurch at once.

scene_surge.narration: Halfway across, a gang of queue-jumpers charges into the water behind you, and a wagon full of bread tips over with a SPLASH. Two river drakes surface at once, very interested in the bread. The current is shoving at your knees.

choices.label: Toss the drakes their toll: the floating bread
Hold the wagon up, whatever the drakes think
Let go and ride the current

check_drake_toll.prompt: Pay the river drakes politely in bread

onSuccess.narration: The drakes take the bread like a toll collector takes coins, and one of them even nudges the wagon back onto its wheels with its nose. Drovers haul you up the north bank by your collars.

onFailure.narration: One drake takes the bread. The other one wanted the bread you were holding, and it bumps you, very gently, into the deep part.

encounter_drakes.narration: The drakes do not see why a wagon full of bread should stay upright when it could be lunch.

onVictory.narration: The drakes sulk off downstream with one loaf each, and the drovers cheer as you all shove the wagon up onto the north bank.

onDefeat.narration: A drake flicks its tail, the wagon goes over, and the whole lot of you go with it, bread and bags and all, off into the current.

end_forded.narration: You stand dripping on the north bank of the west branch, with the whole rush pouring past you toward the mountain. The tuned charm in your pocket is still chiming at every wagon. Behind you, the crossing verse starts again for the next wagon in line. Tonight you camp on the north side, warm and loud and very much in the thick of it.

end_marsh_west.narration: The west branch does what rivers do: it whooshes you west into the green tangles of the Whispering Marsh, past a boggart in a reed hat who applauds. At last the channels let you go on a muddy bank near MossHome, at the flooded edge of the Enchanted Woods. You never chose this road, but here you are, and the tuned charm is still humming. The road people will hear about it. The road people hear about everything.

end_swept_setback.narration: The current takes you a long, long way west, through the marsh's tangles and out the far side, three days later than you meant to arrive anywhere. You wash up on the flooded paths of the Enchanted Woods with wet bags, a cold supper, and a drake-shaped grudge. It is not the road you chose, and it cost you time, but you are all together and the charm is still humming.

llmHints.tone: busy, loud, funny road-camp country; warm underneath, a little spooky at dusk, never scary

npcVoices.burdock: a faun provisioner; cheerful, shameless about his prices, calls everyone 'my lucky number'
npcVoices.tamsin: Tamsin Three-Cards, a kitsune card-sharp; quick, delighted to be caught, never sore about losing
npcVoices.wend: a Deep Hollow soup ladler; gentle, generous, asks nothing, says 'kindness first' and means it a little too much
npcVoices.mother_thrum: a ford witch; careful and instructive, peers over spectacles, always asks 'what do you actually want?'
npcVoices.drover: the lead drover; slow, booming voice, sings the crossing verse and will not be hurried
npcVoices.relay_runner: a centaur relay-runner; talks while galloping, never finishes a sentence in the same place she started it
npcVoices.brackens: the Brackens, a faun family whose season is over; tired, polite, the littlest one very brave about it
